prerequisites: Knowledge in the following subjects: Geometry, trigonometry, differential and integral calculus. Vector calculus. Sliding vectors. Equilibrium of particles and rigid bodies. Friction. Kinematics of particles. Dynamics of particles. Dynamics of particle systems.

syllabus_topics: Topic 6. Energy and momentum methods. Introduction: work of forces acting on a rigid body. Principle of work and energy for a rigid body. Planar motion of a rigid body. Systems of rigid bodies. Constrained planar motion. Conservation of energy. Principle of impulse and momentum for planar motion of a rigid body.

Topic 7. Introduction to Analytical Mechanics. Introduction: virtual displacements and work. Principle of virtual work. Real machines. Mechanical efficiency. D'Alembert's principle. Constraints or linkages. Generalized coordinates. D'Alembert's principle in generalized coordinates. Basic form of Lagrange's equations. Conservative forces: Lagrangian function.

Topic 1. Kinematics of rigid systems. Definition of a rigid system. Theorem of projected velocities. Types of motion of a rigid system. Translational motion. Rotational motion around a fixed axis. General planar motion. Definition of instantaneous center of rotation. Pure rolling motion. Rolling motion with sliding (cam).

Topic 2. Kinematics of relative motion. Vector fixed with respect to a mobile reference system. Vector not fixed to a mobile reference system. Velocity of a particle for different reference systems. Acceleration of a particle for different reference systems. Composition of motions. Formulation of equations in kinematic pairs.

Topic 3. Kinematics of planar motion. Definition and generalities in planar motion. Velocity distribution. Determination of the instantaneous center of rotation. Analytical calculation of velocities using instantaneous center of rotation. Plotting of polar curves. Examples. Types of contact between base and roulette. Velocity of succession of the instantaneous center of rotation. Hartmann's graphical method. Acceleration distribution. Acceleration of the instantaneous center of rotation.

Topic 8. Mechanical transmissions. General concepts. Nomenclature of gear teeth. Gear trains. Planetary gear trains. The formula method. Introduction to belt transmissions. Introduction to chain transmissions.

Topic 5. Dynamics of Mechanisms and Machines. Introduction: particle systems. Rigid bodies. Equations of motion. D'Alembert's principle. Planar motion of a rigid body. Systems of rigid bodies. Constrained planar motion. Rolling motion.

Topic 4. Introduction to mechanism analysis. Definition of Machine and Mechanism. Classification of Machines. Materials used in machine construction. Actions acting on machines. Link and kinematic pair. Kinematic chain and mechanism. Classification and representation of mechanisms. Classification of links. Classification of kinematic pairs. Degrees of freedom of a mechanism. Application of mechanisms. Grashof's Law.

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment activities (Theoretical-practical questionnaires and/or proposed problems)

assessment_rules: The Final Exam (E) accounts for 90% of the grade, and continuous assessment activities (C) account for 10%. The Final Exam is structured as E = 0.3T + 0.3PC + 0.3PD + 0.1PT, where T is the theoretical part, PC is the kinematic analysis problem, PD is the dynamic-kinetic analysis problem, and PT is for other applied theory problems. A minimum score of 3 out of 10 is required for the theoretical part (T) of the final exam, and a minimum of 2.5 out of 10 for problems PC and PD. The final exam is evaluated in its entirety, regardless of the individual part scores.
